newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed with big gains, supported by a fall in German industry orders and initial signs that President Yeltsin's heart surgery had gone well.
The benchmark January 2006 bond closed 0.65 firmer at 101.32/42 for a bid yield of 5.81 percent, a level last seen in January of this year.
Dealers said prices received an initial push from news of a 3.6 percent fall in German September industry orders which followed Monday's news of a fall in German industry output.
This helped to temper fears that strong economic growth will lead to higher interest rates.
Prices rose further, due in part to short-covering, as news came through that Russian President Boris Yeltsin's seven-hour open-heart operation had gone well.
"We were already trading at higher levels and when Yeltsin was reported to be okay, prices came up further," a dealer said.
The firmer tone in U.S. Treasuries as Americans voted in their country's presidential election also helped the market to close at the day's highs.
However some dealers felt that the market was likely to bounce back off its current highs.
"I'm not convinced we can hold these levels. The bund future hit 100 last week but then it quickly came off 70 basis points and I think we'll see the same thing again," said one dealer.
In the long term most players expect a resumption of the recent flattening trend in the yield curve with yields at the long end not moving much but yields at the short end rising.
